planning_notes: Board is Arduino Mega 2560 (as specified). Circuit wiring uses mega:2/3/4 for btn1/btn2/btn3, mega:5/6/7 for rgb1 R/G/B, and mega:8/9 for servo1/servo2 PWM control.

All three push buttons are modeled as active-high inputs (model true when pressed). No pullup/pulldown wiring override was provided; the design assumes the existing circuit provides appropriate electrical stability.
Servo endpoints and timing belong to the SysML model; requests only define initial angle and control pins. Both servos start at 0 degrees after reset.

RGB LED is common cathode per circuit; therefore model true for each color corresponds to electrically driving that color output HIGH (turning it on) and startup sets all colors off (all outputs false).
Each required state (servo angle and RGB color) must be held for at least 2 seconds via SysML timing/elapsed_ms logic; no timing/durations are encoded in device requests.

**Task**:
You are tasked with programming an Arduino (uno) to control two servos (servo1, servo2) and an RGB LED (rgb1) using three push buttons (btn1, btn2, btn3). The RGB LED will display different colors based on the state of the servos, and the push buttons will control the movement of the servos and the color of the RGB LED.

**Detail Rules**:
Initialization: Upon powering on or resetting, both servos (servo1, servo2) should be at their 0-degree position, and the RGB LED (rgb1) should be off.
Button Interaction:
1. The first button (btn1) will rotate servo1 (servo1) to 90 degrees and set the RGB LED (rgb1) to red.
2. The second button (btn2) will rotate servo2 (servo2) to 90 degrees and set the RGB LED (rgb1) to green.
3. The third button (btn3) will reset both servos (servo1, servo2) to their 0-degree position and set the RGB LED (rgb1) to blue.
Each state (servo position and LED color) should be maintained for at least 2 seconds to allow for verification.
